segmentation.text: intending to turn to the left
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Within an intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'Approaching from the opposite direction', per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, is read through the carrier v approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) and its st.lane_direction, opposed to the direction of the carrier c1 the subject entered X from, within p.oncoming_heading_cos — never from current headings, which the subject's turn changes.
'Which is within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies), having come from c2.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

operationalizations.standard: so close to the intersection as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a vehicle approaching on its carrier is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and the subject declares int.left_turn at X (intent subject X) at that observation.
obligation: Re-binding X as in the applicability, and c1 as the carrier entering X (st.lane_enters c1 X) the subject occupied when it last entered X (it has overlapped X continuously since an observation at which it occupied c1): for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle approaching from the opposite direction — v occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2, where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos — and that either overlaps X or, on c2, has its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlaps X and declares int.left_turn at X; v approaches on c2, whose st.lane_direction is opposed to that of the subject's entry carrier c1; the subject moves into its turn with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance while its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject stays at rest in X until v has passed, then turns.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses X with int.left_turn declared false at X (its plan goes straight).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Left-turning subject in X, opposing v in conflict; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject turns left in X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v approaches from a cross street (its carrier's direction perpendicular to c1's) on a conflicting path; the subject turns: v does not approach from the opposite direction.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: skew tolerance of opposing intersection approaches
